parts.text:
A moon is in circular orbit around a planet.

Explain why the path of the moon is circular.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Many moons are in circular orbit about a planet.

The angular velocity of a moon is $\omega$ when the orbit of the moon has a radius $r$ about the planet.

Fig. 1.2 shows the variation of $r^3$ with $1/\omega^2$ for these moons.

{{figure:figure_1_2.png}}

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text:
Show that the mass $M$ of the planet is given by
$$M = \frac{\text{gradient}}{G}$$
where $G$ is the gravitational constant.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Use Fig. 1.2 and the expression in (c)(i) to show that the mass $M$ of the planet is $1.0 \times 10^{26}\text{ kg}$.
